analysis.title: GS Callahan - US TMT Quick Hits 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: NDX rallied back to roughly unchanged on the day, recapturing its 50-day and 100-day moving averages, but sentiment remains weak after back-to-back difficult sessions.
GS TMT Momentum Pairs fell about 12% over 2 days and were lower on 8 of the last 9 sessions.
Semis closed lower for 7 straight sessions, the biggest 7-day pullback since 'liberation day'.
Risk appetite is challenged, with signs of risk-off price action and flows as investors weigh several issues in a compressed calendar window into year-end.
Long-end yields reset lower as the curve flattened (10yr = 5.08%), and MU finished +2%, yet NDX up with yields down made daily price action hard to read given positioning and momentum wobbles.

Unlike the July momentum unwind, which the desk called technical after the April-June run, the current episode raises debate over which 'wall of worry' is most acute: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation, product momentum.

Client conversations this week: fewer questions on trading 'innings', more on thematic and fundamental conviction. Big tech remains topical and well liked. More willingness to play offense on both long and short sides. More questions on where to weather volatility besides Apple.
The desk says it is hard to read much into the TSM and ASML prints given the tape.
Top client questions today: defensives people like, feedback on the TSM print, NFLX up 7 of 9 days and expectations, gaming ecosystem (RBLX, TTWO, Unity, APP), and the vibe on Memory.
The NDX forward P/E is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, which the desk frames as a possible supportive backdrop for earnings to do some work in earnings season.
The NDX is testing its trendline from the March lows.
earnings_insights: The desk says it is hard to read much into the TSM and ASML prints given the tape. Clients asked for feedback on the TSM print and on NFLX expectations after it rose 7 of 9 days.
